items.title: Serbia just elected the world's brainiest parliament
items.summary: After the student-led opposition movement Student List - Students Are Winning won Serbia's October 25 parliamentary election with 141 of 250 seats, dozens of its representatives come from academia and more than half hold a Ph.D. or M.D. The group emerged from nationwide protests over corruption and now must form a government after 13 years of rule under Aleksandar Vučić, promising to fight corruption, restore academic autonomy, and boost science funding.

items.title: French lawmakers approved a tax of €0.055 for every gigabyte of internet traffic
items.summary: On Friday night the French National Assembly adopted amendment 1358 to the 2027 budget bill in a 11-10 vote, creating a tax on digital data flows emitted by content providers. Its sponsor, Laurent Lhardit, estimated the levy would raise about 10 billion euros and argued it would be paid almost entirely by large global tech platforms, whose traffic makes up most of what reaches French internet subscribers.

items.title: Switch Lowering in GCC
items.summary: A detailed walkthrough of how GCC turns C switch statements into machine code at -O3: jump tables, offset adjustments for constant case values, decision trees, and bitset lowering. Using annotated disassembly, the post shows GCC only converts a switch to a jump table when there are roughly eight or more jump table entries per case label, and notes most of these optimizations translate to Clang except the bitset lowering.
